messages:
anya: Hey team — heads up: I need to swap my primary shift tomorrow 07:00-15:00 UTC due to a brief medical appointment. I want to make sure we don’t have a coverage gap during morning ramp. Can someone pick up primary for 07:00-11:00 or take a split? @jamal @mike?

oncall-bot: PAGER: embeds-queue latency spike — Sev3 — 2024-11-02T06:12Z — PagerID: P-8823. Pager delivered to #eng-oncall.

jamal: I can take primary 07:00-11:00 UTC. Quick question — any ongoing mitigations I should be aware of? Where’s the runbook for embeds?

sre-runbooks: Runbook link: https://r.runbooks/redwood/embeds-latency — TL;DR: check redis queue depth, restart embed-workers if queue_depth > 500, verify KV cache hit rate, escalate to perf if error_rate > 10%. Also see mitigation steps below.

mike: I can shadow 07:00-09:00 and then join handoff to jamal at 10:45. @anya do you have any active customer tickets pinned?

anya: Thanks all. No high-priority tickets pinned — the console shows a recurring embed backoff that self-resolves. I left notes in my handoff doc: https://docs.redwood/handovers/anya-2024-11-02. Also: please confirm you can trigger the cold restart if needed — creds in 1Password.

anya: restart snippet (paste this if you need to restart workers):

sre-runbooks: ```
# restart embed workers on pool-a
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deploy/embed-workers-pool-a
# sanity checks (run after ~30s)
curl -sS https://internal-metrics/embeds | jq '.queue_depth, .error_rate, .inflight_requests'
```

mike: Got it, I’m comfortable running the rollout if we hit the threshold. I’ll capture logs and S3 snapshots before restart.

jamal: Confirmed — I’ll be primary 07:00-11:00 UTC. Will enable pager forwarding and update rota.

oncall-bot: @jamal set as primary for shift 07:00-11:00 UTC. Pager forwarding active. :white_check_mark:

lina: I can cover 11:00-15:00 UTC if jamal needs to hand off early — travel might free me sooner, otherwise I’ll be on standby as secondary.

anya: Amazing, thank you. @mike can you be the handover watcher 09:00-11:00 so jamal isn’t solo during the morning ramp? Please call out if you need a second shadow.

mike: Affirmative. I’ll join the handoff at 10:45 and keep shadow until 11:15 to make the transition smooth.

jamal: I’ll update the calendar and add the runbook pointer to the incident bridge. Also pinging perf: @perf-oncall FYI in case we need deeper kernel/driver-level investigation for sustained spikes.

anya: Handoff checklist (brief):
1) Enable pager forwarding to primary (jamal).
2) Share runbook link (done).
3) 1Password path with restart creds: Ops/Oncall/Embed-Restarts (I’ll DM @mike).
4) Customer notes: Customer-A and Customer-B saw ~2-3 requests fail during the spike, no data loss.
5) If queue depth grows after restart, escalate to perf and open a postmortem ticket.

mike: Where exactly is the 1Password entry? I’ll need checkout rights.

anya: 1Password: Ops/Oncall/Embed-Restarts — I’ll DM the temporary access now.

jamal: Added notes to the bridge and the calendar. Also set a quick reminder at 06:50 UTC for pre-shift check (metrics, outgoing deploys).

lina: If jamal needs to drop earlier, I’ll move my 11:00 start to 10:30 — ping in this thread and I’ll jump in.

jamal: Good plan. Also putting a small note: if we do the restart, keep an eye on cache warmup — error rate can transiently spike for ~2-5 minutes. If error_rate > 15% post-restart, escalate to perf immediately.

oncall-bot: Reminder: Next rotation boundary at 11:00 UTC. To request an automated swap, mention the bot with exact shift window. See `@oncall-bot help swaps`.

anya: Thanks everyone — I’ll DM the creds and mark this as covered. Leaving the thread open for any last-minute updates. :pray:
